editorial:
Imagine you are about to start high school and your older brother tells you it is basically a nightmare. That is exactly where Cj finds herself. She is terrified of losing her spark and watching her best friends, Fen and Crispo, drift away as they start caring about cooler things. To fight this fear, she makes a massive bucket list of 100 things to do before middle school ends. The whole vibe is super lighthearted and sweet, capturing that weird feeling of being a kid but wanting to grow up fast. It feels like a warm hug of a movie that reminds you how important it is to just have fun with your friends.

The acting is surprisingly natural, and the pacing keeps you moving through the list without feeling bored. While it is a bit predictable since it is a family movie, the heart is definitely there. You will love it if you enjoy coming-of-age stories that do not take themselves too seriously.
endingExplained: By the end, Cj realizes that checking off every single item on her list is not as important as the memories she made. She learns that high school does not have to be scary as long as she stays true to herself. The friends reconcile and realize their bond is stronger than any social pressure. It wraps up with a sweet graduation feel, showing that growing up is okay when you have a good support system.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves cute stories about friendship and growing up.
